name: Wallfahrtsort Mariastein
kurzbeschreibung: The pilgrimage site of Mariastein in Kufsteinerland: a Gothic tower castle on a 14 m rock cone, 150 steps to the Chapel of Grace and guardian of the 1602 Tyrolean Archducal Hat.
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular pilgrimage site of Mariastein is situated in the municipality of the same name in the Tyrolean Unterinntal, just a few kilometres north of Wörgl and Kufstein at an altitude of approximately 575 metres. Presenting a unique symbiosis of a fortified medieval tower castle and a sacred pilgrimage sanctuary, the building perches boldly atop a freestanding, 14-metre-high rock cone of pale dolomite. With its 42-metre-high, battlemented keep, the architectural ensemble attracts art enthusiasts, pilgrims, and history lovers alike, preserving one of the most precious secular and religious relics of the state of Tyrol.

History & Castle Museum

The origins of the complex date back to the 14th century: around the year 1361, the powerful Lords of Freundsberg built the fortified castle to monitor the ancient Roman road along the left bank of the Inn river. A legendary occurrence in the 15th century transformed the stronghold into a renowned pilgrimage destination far beyond the region: following an arson attempt during the Bavarian Peasants' War, the Gothic miraculous image of the Virgin Mary is said to have remained miraculously unscathed. When the castle lord repeatedly had the statue returned to his private chapel, it continuously reappeared in a miraculous manner on the highest rock. Consequently, the Gnadenkapelle Mariastein was built on the topmost storey of the tower. Pilgrims climb up to the chapel via the Heilige Stiege – a steep wooden staircase with exactly 150 steps, symbolizing the 150 Hail Marys of the traditional Rosary. Beside the spiritual pilgrimage site, the castle tower houses the remarkable Schlossmuseum Mariastein: the crowning jewel of the princely treasury is Tyrol's official state sanctuary – the Tiroler Erzherzogshut. This splendid, pearl-studded coronet was donated in 1602 by the Tyrolean sovereign Maximilian III. der Deutschmeister and to this day symbolizes the historical sovereignty of the land. Also displayed are the gilded imperial sceptre of Emperor Matthias, valuable votive tablets, and medieval armour pieces.

Visit & Getting There

The castle courtyard and the pilgrimage chapel in the tower are freely accessible daily throughout the year from 08:00 to 18:00 (in summer until 19:00). Admission to the pilgrimage church is free of charge (donations for the maintenance of the monument are appreciated). The historic castle museum housing the Archducal Hat is open daily from May to October between 09:00 and 17:00; museum admission: adults approx. €5.00, children approx. €2.50 (discounted with the KufsteinerlandCard). Arrival by car: Via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wörgl Ost or Kufstein Süd), continuing along the country road via Angerberg directly to Mariastein (large free parking areas are available at the base of the castle rock). By public transport: ÖBB trains to Wörgl Hauptbahnhof or Kufstein, from where regional VVT bus line 4068 runs hourly directly to the Mariastein Wallfahrtskirche bus stop.

Tips

Access to the castle courtyard and lower church is step-free and barrier-friendly; the ascent to the upper Chapel of Grace and the museum is via the historic staircase (150 steps) and is unfortunately not suitable for wheelchairs. After your visit, the time-honoured Mariasteiner Hof or the castle café offer delightful Tyrolean Krapfen pastries and refreshments. Combine your excursion with a scenic walk across the idyllic Angerberg high plateau.
